findings.text: When a class already has __rich_repr__ defined and uses @auto(angular=True), the angular attribute is never set on the existing method (line 122 is inside the if block). This causes auto_repr to read angular=False via getattr's default, ignoring the decorator argument. Failing input: a class with existing __rich_repr__ decorated with @auto(angular=True).

The auto_rich_repr function yields getattr(self, name) for POSITIONAL_ONLY parameters without verifying the attribute exists. If __init__ doesn't store a parameter as an instance attribute, repr() will raise ReprError. Failing input: a class where __init__ has a positional-only parameter that isn't assigned to self.
